findings.title: Unhealthy flusher processes are never killed because the isinstance check misses SpawnProcess
findings.body: Processes are created with `multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process`, so each one is a `SpawnProcess`. `SpawnProcess` subclasses `BaseProcess`, not `multiprocessing.Process`, so `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` is always False in production. The old code called `kill()` unconditionally; with the new guard, a hung flusher is never killed. A replacement process is still spawned for the same shards, so two processes flush the same shards at once. That can produce duplicate or fragmented segments, and leaked processes pile up with each restart. Check for `multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess` instead, or check `not isinstance(process, threading.Thread)`. The same wrong check in `join()` (line 346) means `terminate()` is never called either.

findings.title: join() stops early and skips terminating the remaining processes once the deadline passes
findings.body: When the deadline is exceeded, the loop does `break`. Every process after that point is left without `terminate()` being called. This happens often, because `next_step.join(timeout)` runs first and can use up most of the timeout. Those flusher processes keep running past consumer shutdown or rebalance and may still touch Redis and Kafka for shards that are no longer assigned. The loop should skip the waiting but still terminate every remaining process.

findings.title: Restart limit is now counted per process, so total allowed restarts scales with process count
findings.body: `MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS` used to cap the total number of flusher restarts before the consumer is failed. It is now tracked separately for each process index. With N processes, the consumer tolerates up to N*(MAX+1) crashes before raising, which weakens the crash-loop safeguard.

findings.title: Inconsistent metric tag key: 'shards' here vs 'shard' elsewhere
findings.body: `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` is tagged with `shards`, while `flusher.produce`, `segment_size_bytes` and `flusher_unhealthy` use `shard`. Dashboards and queries that filter or group by `shard` will miss this metric. In addition, the tag value is a comma-joined list of shards (e.g. "0,4,8") on some metrics and a single shard elsewhere, which adds tag cardinality and makes the values inconsistent.

findings.title: Docstring claims one process per shard, but the CLI default is a single process
findings.body: The class docstring says it "Creates one process per shard". The `--flusher-processes` CLI option defaults to 1, so in production all shards share a single process unless the option is set explicitly. One process per shard only happens when `max_processes` is None or 0.

findings.title: Added time.sleep(0.1) is a no-op because time.sleep is monkeypatched
findings.body: The test monkeypatches `time.sleep` to `lambda _: None`, so the new `time.sleep(0.1)`, meant to "give flusher threads time to process", does nothing. The test still relies on the flusher thread happening to flush before it sees `stopped` in `join()`. It therefore stays timing-dependent and potentially flaky, despite the comment suggesting otherwise.
